bats use caves as hibernation sites in temperate regions, and that the level of activity in caves is related to the temperature of the hibernation site.

(i) bats are the only group in which some members have successfully exploited caves for shelter throughout all year; (ii) caves are used by bats as a hibernaculum during winter; (iii) bats use the caves as a hibernation site, and the most important factors affecting their choice of hibernaculum are temperature, humidity and size of the cave, and (iv) white‐nose disease has been a significant threat to cave‐dwel‐ ling bats.
